decks.thematic: Every Action card in the game. Actions are the shared tactical layer - stealth, theft, rumours, and practical tricks that no faction owns.
Every Event card in the game. Events are the one-shot pressures and opportunities that push a turn off its expected line.
Every Land card in the game. Lands are the places a run passes through, each carrying its own terrain and flavour.
Every Population Centre card in the game. PCs are the holdings a faction builds from and fights over.
Every Character card in the game, from named heroes to minor agents, with their commander/agent/emissary/mage ratings.
Every Army card in the game - troop types, their special abilities, and the costs to field them.
Every Ally card in the game: the powers and creatures that can be brought to a side rather than commanded outright.
Every Spell card in the game, from lightweight magical flourishes to the workings of the great powers.
Every Environmental card in the game - weather, seasons, and the moods of the land that touch every side at once.
Every Object card in the game: rings, blades, palantiri, and lesser treasures, each granting effects while held.

High-authority comeback deck built around renewal, courage, cleansing, and open leadership after the return in white. This deck should reward stabilization, morale swings, anti-fear and anti-corruption play, stronger army support, and decisive rally turns; it suits players who want to absorb pressure, reclaim control, and then swing the board through righteous momentum.

Pure wizardry deck focused on refined spellcraft, insight, wards, lore, and precise magical intervention. Elven wisdom, hidden knowledge, vision, revelation, and tightly targeted magic all belong here; in gameplay it emphasizes selective control, information advantage, safe setup, and elegant spell resolution rather than broad swarm or raw military output.

Orren Stormherald is the Orren Greycloak subdeck of uneasy wartime pressure among Men. It should frame the Grey Wanderer not only as an ill omen or unwelcome counselor, but as the unsettling force who appears when Mannish realms are strained by encroaching evil and must harden themselves for survival. This includes fronts such as Mearhold against the White Hand, Ardanth against Morgahd, the Northmen of Wildermark against Easterners, the Longwater Vale against Dol Vorrath, Crossway and wider the Marches under the long memory of Grimhold, and similar regions where roads, ports, fords, courts, and frontier settlements live under gathering shadow. Orren Greycloak is trying to help, organize, and strengthen resistance, yet many still see him as the sign that peace has already failed. In gameplay the deck should lean into morale strain, defensive hardening, political tension, frontier vigilance, war-readiness, movement pressure, intelligence and concealment, loyalty under stress, and reputation-based disruption rather than reducing itself to repeated warnings or bad-news delivery.

Mischief, adventure, and social-chaos deck built around hollowkin, roadside incidents, strange meetings, awkward interruptions, and unexpectedly powerful small-scale plays. Its regional flavor should stretch across the Marches, especially Crossway-land, the roads and inns of the North, the The Elderwood, the The Cairnfields, scattered settlements, and out toward Caldwold, so the deck can hold wandering locals, petty troublemakers, rural rumors, travel incidents, eerie borderland hazards, and small but meaningful frontier entanglements. It is less martial than other branches and more about quirky utility, board disturbance, off-angle events, and playful disruption that feels fair but annoying for the opponent.

Dwarf-friend archetype rooted in mountains, halls, treasure, mithril, endurance, and old alliances with the Durn folk. Expect Dwarven races, Erenkarr and Khazad themes, defensive economy, sturdy progression, fortress-like value, and reward for treasure or mountain cards; this deck suits slow-building players who want resilience, gear, and hard-to-shift board presence.

Thornspire mastermind deck focused on rhetoric, control, persuasion, voice, and polished strategic dominance. This is Vaskar as the calculating high wizard who bends choices and states rather than simply rushing with troops; players should expect influence, deception, mind-affecting actions, elegant tactical denial, and carefully timed control cards.

Arcane self-reinvention deck expressing Vaskar's many-coloured identity: layered wizardry, vanity, broad magical reach, and power drawn from synthesis rather than purity. This subdeck is ideal for spell-oriented play with multi-axis magical effects, buffs and debuffs in the same action, symbolic robes-and-voice flavor, and flashy board manipulation that feels sophisticated and dangerous.

War engine of Thornspire built around Graukh, Orc industry, furnaces, intimidation, and relentless production-to-pressure conversion. This is the aggressive Vaskar branch: siege tools, military events, battlefield force multiplication, and sustained assault through disciplined evil infantry and industrial throughput rather than finesse.

The fallen Vaskar as Sharrow, master of the Thornhollow's ruffians. This subdeck is about coercion, intimidation, and petty cruelty: agent and emissary tactics that dominate civilian settlements through fear, pipe-weed monopoly, and Skeil's whispered betrayals. No magic remains — only spite, cunning, and the relentless grinding-down of everything pleasant.

Lidless surveillance and Wraithlords command deck centered on dread presence, revelation, control auras, and the feeling that no movement escapes Morgahd's notice. It favors fear, despair, board locking, command projection, cursed riders, and oppressive events that squeeze the opponent's options turn by turn until resistance becomes inefficient.

Subversion-and-false-gifts deck for Nharok as Annatar and corrupter: persuasive command, fallen Andarim legacy, seeing-stone theft, temptation, and domination achieved through trust, seduction, and crooked counsel before open conquest.

Dol Vorrath horror deck built around dark sorcery, ruined strongholds, cursed creatures, lingering effects, and monster-heavy occult pressure. Goblins, spirits, spiders, dragons, undead presences, and slow magical decay all fit here; gameplay leans toward attrition, haunting pressure, corruption-adjacent status play, and a more monstrous, supernatural style than the disciplined Dark Eye branch.

Eastern shadow and dark diplomacy deck built around Nharok's influence over the Easterner tribes beyond the Sea of Rhûn. It favors horde raising through emissary pressure, whispered threats, iron promises, and the patient swelling of eastern war-bands that look westward with hungry patience.

Witch-realm of Grimhold deck centered on the Witch-king's iron crown: deception, slaving, and the breaking of hope among the Men of the Marches. It breeds Orcs and Trolls from northern mountain holds, gnaws at Ardwyn and Caldwold through false counsel and terror, and pours dark sorcery from Carn Dûm like a black river that bends wills before blades are drawn.
